approach: Add one shared private const CHECKABLE_CRITERIA_RULE to briefs.rs. Render it in the reader brief as its own `# Checkable criteria` section (after the code survey guide, before `# What the verifier can run`), so READING_RULES and its tests are untouched. Render it in the producer brief as a new `## Make your evidence checkable` section (fn checkable_evidence_section) just before criteria_check_section. The producer section says: prefer a test in the change; add a file only when a deliverable or criterion names it; the report is still where you state what you ran or read; a criterion provable only from the report is reported unmet with the note that the verifier cannot check it. Two tests render the briefs and assert on their text. In structure-pass.md section 5, every report-held proof becomes something in the snapshot: the committed tests and code, which the verifier builds and runs, plus a rerun command or diff check the verifier does itself. Item 5 says the proof is in the snapshot (committed tests compile and run every hit, the 5.1 test covers the PrHost fakes) and the verifier reruns the old-path Grep and reads `git diff -U0 -- crates/`; stored before/after counts are dropped because a stored 'before' count cannot be rechecked. 5.2 points at the existing introspect.rs test. No new evidence file or docs note, so items 1, 4 and 7 stay true. One CHANGELOG line. No refusal logic, prompt file or governance file changes.

decisions.choice: New standalone `# Checkable criteria` section in the reader brief, not a ninth READING_RULES line
decisions.reason: READING_RULES is [&str; 8] and tests (~4476-4521) assert len 8, one check named per line, lines <=220 bytes and the section <2600 bytes. The rule adds no check (check_criteria_evidence stays as is). Its own `# ` heading ends the rules section at the next `\n# `, so those tests read the same text.

rejected.why: Breaks the len==8 and 'each rule names a check' assertions and needs edits to existing tests.

rejected.option: Append the sentence to the 'What the verifier can run' paragraph
rejected.why: That section prints only when verifier_can_run is non-empty and an existing test covers its wording; the rule should always show and existing wording must stay unchanged.

rejected.option: Edit prompts/reader.md or the producer prompt
rejected.why: Reader headroom is 3 tokens, budgets are fixed and prompt files are out of scope.

decisions.choice: The reader section does not point at 'the list below'. It says each criterion's check names a file, a diff line or a command the verifier can run (listed under What the verifier can run when given).
decisions.reason: The list prints only when verifier_can_run is non-empty (briefs.rs ~2426) while the new section must always show.

rejected.why: The list can be absent, leaving a dangling reference.

decisions.choice: Producer section text (answers finding 3 and 4): the shared rule; 'Prefer a test in your change that shows the property. Add a new file for evidence only when a deliverable or a criterion names it. Your report is still where you state what you ran or read; the rule only means the verifier does not rely on it. If a criterion can be shown only from your report, report it unmet and say the verifier cannot check it; do not invent a file.' Status chosen: unmet.
decisions.reason: criteria_check_section (briefs.rs 746-760) requires every non-left-to-Athena criterion to be reported met with evidence of what you ran or read, so the new text must give the uncheckable case a status. Unmet is honest (the verifier cannot confirm it) and the existing send-back handling then surfaces the problem instead of letting a met claim pass unchecked. The extra sentence makes the report-still-states-what-you-ran claim true, so the risk mitigation quotes real text. Test asserts 'report it unmet' and 'the verifier cannot check it'.

rejected.option: Keep it 'met' and add a note for the verifier
rejected.why: A met status on a criterion the verifier cannot check is the failure this change is meant to stop.

rejected.option: Tell every producer to commit a counts or notes file for non-diff proof
rejected.why: Stray files break file-scope criteria such as criterion 6 and unchanged_files_section comparisons (briefs.rs ~770).

decisions.choice: Producer wording says 'in your change' / 'in the candidate', never 'commit'
decisions.reason: The working-directory text (briefs.rs ~657) says 'Your edits become the candidate' and Athena owns commits.

rejected.why: Contradicts the working-directory text and may prompt git commit attempts.

decisions.choice: One shared private const used by both briefs
decisions.reason: The two briefs cannot drift; each test asserts the literal phrase written in the test, not the constant.

rejected.option: Write the rule separately in each brief

decisions.choice: Item 5 (answers finding 1): wording makes the evidence plainly part of the snapshot. Text: 'Caller check. The proof is in the snapshot, not in the report: every hit of each moved name's old path (for example gh::GhClient, gh::land_pr, run::send_back_text) over crates/ is compiled and run by the committed tests (cargo test --locked), and the fake hosts implementing PrHost are covered by the test named in 5.1. The verifier reruns the Grep for each old path over crates/ on the candidate and reads git diff -U0 -- crates/, which must show no line holding an old path removed or added outside moved blocks. No before/after count is stored: a stored before count cannot be rechecked.'
decisions.reason: Criterion 3 asks that the caller-check evidence be in the snapshot (a committed file or test). The committed tests and code are the snapshot evidence, and the rerun makes it checkable. A new file or note is blocked by items 4 and 7, and new test lines by item 1, so the existing committed tests are the only snapshot evidence that does not break another item. The conflict between 'file or test' and items 1/4/7 is recorded as an open question for the user.

rejected.option: A committed note under docs/ with before/after counts
rejected.why: Items 4 and 7 forbid extra docs changes, and a stored 'before' count is still the producer's claim the verifier cannot recheck.

rejected.option: A new test with a `use` line for each old path
rejected.why: Item 1 allows only `use` line changes in existing tests; a new test conflicts with 'same tests, unedited'.

rejected.option: Say only 'the verifier reruns the Grep' with no mention of the snapshot
rejected.why: Reads as not meeting criterion 3, which asks for the evidence in the snapshot.

decisions.choice: Rewrite the other report-held proofs the same way: item 2, item 3, the two R5-R8 bullets, the 5.2 'both runs' sentence, the 5.2 'job repeats the Grep' sentence, the item 5 'job names the test' tail, and row 294 of 5.1
decisions.reason: The Grep `report` check must show no requirement whose proof lives only in the report. Item 2: the verifier reruns `cargo test --locked -p athena-core -- --list` on the candidate; item 1's diff check (no test line added or removed except `use`) shows names unchanged, so no count is stored. Item 3: the verifier reads `git diff -M --color-moved=zebra`; every line not marked moved must be a `mod`, `use`, `pub use` or visibility line. R5-R8: the diff shows each removed `return Ok(closing)` with a `Flow::Stop` added in its place, counted from `git diff`, and each local that crossed a seam is a named field in the added struct. 5.2: the guard's self-tests in external_calls_guard.rs run on the candidate, and the existing introspect.rs test `a_landing_touching_a_file_under_gh_selects_d87_and_d88` (line 1707, asserts `selected_by_path(...) == ["D87","D88"]` at 1715) is run by name on the candidate; the verifier reruns the Grep. Row 294 becomes 'the early-return pairing read in the diff'.

rejected.why: Leaves items 2, 3, the R5-R8 bullets and 5.2 report-only, failing the Grep `report` check.

rejected.option: Have 5.2 ask each job to commit a new D87/D88 selection test (previous plan)
rejected.why: Finding 2: breaks item 1, and the test already exists at introspect.rs:1707.

decisions.choice: No new refusal or matching check
decisions.reason: The request is a stated rule with a test; check_criteria_evidence already refuses criteria citing the report. No refusal_corpus case or refusal-rate change is involved.

rejected.option: Extend check_criteria_evidence to refuse 'change description' wording
rejected.why: Out of scope; needs replay and corpus work.

decisions.choice: Show file scope (criterion 6) with `git diff --stat` and `git status`
decisions.reason: Both are in the verifier's allowed commands and list any extra touched file directly.

rejected.why: Tests do not detect an extra edited file.

risks.risk: A rewritten item lowers the strength of its check (for example item 2 loses its count).
risks.mitigation: Each replacement is a command the verifier runs itself (`--list`, the old-path Grep) plus a diff check, which is checkable and at least as strong as a count in a report.

open_questions: User: Criterion 3 asks that item 5 put the old-path Grep counts 'in the snapshot (a committed file or test)'. Items 1, 4 and 7 of structure-pass.md forbid a new test line, a new note or another docs change in a structure-pass job, so this plan makes the snapshot evidence the existing committed tests (which compile and run every hit) plus a Grep rerun and a diff check the verifier runs, and drops stored before/after counts because a stored 'before' count cannot be rechecked. Is that acceptable, or should item 5 instead require a committed counts file and relax items 4 and 7 for it?
